newsitem.title: USA: BP in refinery deal with AspenTech.
newsitem.headline: BP in refinery deal with AspenTech.

text.p: BP Oil International, a unit of British Petroleum plc, said Thursday that it has a deal with Aspen Technology to introduce technology in its refineries worldwide, with the aim of significantly improving profit margins.

The deal initially covers three BP refineries -- the Toldeo, Ohio plant, NOREFCO in the Netherlands and RVI in Germany -- but will eventually extend to all BP's wholly-owned plants as well as those it operates jointly with Mobil Corp and others.

"What we've signed is a $5 million deal for the first three plants," said Toni Lee Rudnicki, an Aspen official. "But this is the largest agreement signed at this level looking at a five-year time frame..., covering 32 plants worldwide."
BP has 13 refineries globally which will be covered by the deal, as well as five joint ventures with Mobil and another 14 joint ventures with other partners.
The Aspen advance control and optimisation software and systems is aimed at tightening up the refineries' economics condiserably in terms of the physical operation of the plants.
Together with other BP refinery improvements in place, "the goal is to achieve a profit improvement of $0.50 a barrel of crude oil," the two companies said in a statement.
Considering its recent acquisition of Bechtel PIMS, AspenTech also would aim to introduce that unit's complementary refinery economics optimisation software, Rudnicki said.
